 --------------------------------------------------------------
 Crl.M.Appl. No.1 of 2024  in  Crl. Appeal No.171 of 2024  ---------------------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 8th day of November 2024  ORDER

This is an application filed under Section 430(1) of the Bharathiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023,
seeking suspension of sentence of the applicant/accused in S.C. No.374 of 2019 on the file of the Sadhaque vs State Of Kerala on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182315210/
1 Court of Session, Thrissur.
The applicant/accused has been found guilty for the offences punishable under Sections 450, 376(2)(f) and 506(i) IPC.
The applicant/accused has been sentenced to varying terms of imprisonment for the aforesaid offences.
The sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
Therefore, the maximum period of imprisonment that the applicant/accused will have to undergo is for a period of 10 years.

2. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant/accused that a reading of the impugned judgment will clearly show that PW1, the victim who was a major, had consented to the sexual relationship with the accused.
She became pregnant and it was only after the birth of the child, the complaint was given.
The paternity of the child came under dispute and it was in such circumstances, the false complaint was given against the applicant/accused.

3. It is submitted by the learned Public Prosecutor that the DNA report shows that the applicant/accused is the father of the child and hence the case of the prosecution is substantiated by scientific evidence also.
It is also pointed out that there was no consent on the part of PW1, the victim, and it was due to fear that she had opened the door as opined by the trial court in the impugned judgment.
Therefore, no grounds for suspending the sentence is made out, goes the argument.

4. Heard both sides.
5. Admittedly, PW1 was a major and a married lady with a child.
In such circumstances, the stand taken by PW1 that she was unaware that she was pregnant till she delivered the child cannot be believed.

According to the prosecution case, a gold bracelet had been given by PW1 to the accused and on the pretext of returning the same he had knocked at the door of the victim at midnight and he threatened her that if she did not open the door he would say that it was as per her invite or request that he had come there.
It was due to this threat and fear of humiliation that she had opened the door and let the accused inside her house.
According to the prosecution case, it is thereafter the accused entered her room and committed rape on her.
In the facts and circumstances discussed in the impugned judgment, I find that the applicant/accused has an arguable case.

v) If the conviction and sentence of the applicant/accused is upheld or even modified,
the time during which he is so released shall be excluded in computing the term of his sentence as provided in Section 430(4) BNSS.
vi)
It is also made clear that if any of the conditions are violated, the bail shall stand cancelled.

Sd/-
C.S.SUDHA NP JUDGE 08-11-2024 /True Copy/

opennyai_summary.decision:
In such circumstances and in the interest of justice, the sentence imposed on the applicant/accused is suspended till the disposal of the appeal subject to the following conditions:-
i) The applicant/accused shall be released on bail on executing a bond for 50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the trial court;
ii) He shall deposit half of the total fine amount within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
iii) He shall not commit any offence(s) while on bail;
iv) The applicant/accused shall not in any way contact or attempt to contact the victim or her family member(s) in any manner;
